source_text: Ἐφίστησι τῇ τοῦ Σίμωνος οἰκίᾳ ὁ σωτὴρ καὶ εὑρίσκει πυρέττουσαν τὴν αὐτοῦ πενθεράν· >καὶ ἐπιστὰς ἐπετίμησε τῷ πυρετῷ, καὶ ἀφῆκεν . Μήποτε οὖν ἐν μὲν τῷ· ἀφῆκεν αὐτὴν ὁ πυρετὸς< εἰρημένῳ ὑπὸ Ματθαίου καὶ Μάρκου καὶ ὅλη τῇ πράσει οὐδὲν ὡς περὶ ζῴου ἐμφαίνεται τοῦ τὸν πυρετὸν ἐνεργοῦντος, ἐν δὲ τῷ· >ἐπιστὰς ἐπάνω ἐπετίμησε τῷ πυρετῷ καὶ ἀφῆκεν> εἰρημένῳ ὑπὸ Λουκᾶ οὐκ οἶδα, εἰ μὴ ἀναγκασθησόμεθα τὸ ἐπιτιμώμενον καὶ καὶ ἀφιὲν ζῷον μὴ χωροῦν τὴν τοῦ ἐπιτιμῶντος ἐνέργειαν· ἄψυχον γὰρ καὶ μὴ αἰσθανόμενον ἐπιτιμίας ἐπιτιμᾶσθαι οὐκ εὔλογον λέγειν. Οὐδὲν δὲ θαυμαστὸν εἶναί τινας κακωτικὰς τοῦ ἀνθρωπίνου σώματος δυνάμεις, καὶ οὐ πάντως κατηγορήσωμεν τῆς ψυχῆς τῶν πασχόντων ὡς ἐκ τούτων βλαπτομένης· οὐδὲ γάρ, ἐπεὶ ἔπαισε τὸν Ἰὼβ ἕλκει πονηρῷ λαβὼν ὁ διάβολος τὴν ἐξουσίαν τὸ τὸ διὰ τοῦ σώματος πειράσαι αὐτόν, περὶ τοῦτο κατηγορητέος ὁ Ἰὼβ ἀθλήσας καὶ γενναίως ὑπομείνας τὴν πληγήν. Μόνον εἴη λέγεσθαι, εἴ ποτε κατὰ σωματικοὺς πειραζόμεθα πόνους, τό· ἀλλὰ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ μὴ , ὡς καὶ ὁ κύριος ἐπιτιμῶν ἰᾶται τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας. >᾿ ἀντὶ τοῦ >πέταξεν<.
pass_a_gloss: The Saviour stands at the house of Simon and finds his mother-in-law fevered: and standing he rebuked the fever, and it left. Perhaps then in the The fever left her said by Matthew and Mark and in the whole phrasing nothing appears as about a living being working the fever, but in the Standing over he rebuked the fever and it left, said by Luke, I do not know, unless we shall be compelled [to say] that the thing rebuked and leaving is a living being not containing the working of the one rebuking; for it is not reasonable to say that a soulless thing not perceiving a rebuke is rebuked. Nothing marvellous that there are some powers harmful to the human body, and we shall not altogether accuse the soul of those suffering as harmed from these; for neither, since the devil, having taken the authority to test him through the body, struck Job with an evil sore, is Job to be accused concerning this, having contended and nobly endured the blow. Only let it be said, if ever we are tested by bodily pains, the: but not his soul [touch], as also the Lord rebuking heals those faring badly. [Rebuked] in place of commanded.
pass_b_english: The Saviour comes to Simon's house and finds his mother-in-law sick with fever: “And standing over her he rebuked the fever, and it left her” (Luke 4:39).

Perhaps, then, in “the fever left her”, as Matthew and Mark tell it (Matthew 8:15; Mark 1:31), nothing in the whole wording points to a living being that was producing the fever. But in “standing over her he rebuked the fever, and it left her”, as Luke tells it, I do not see how we can avoid being compelled to say that what is rebuked and departs is a living being that could not withstand the power of the one rebuking it. For it is not reasonable to say that something without a soul, which cannot perceive a rebuke, is rebuked.

It is nothing strange that there are certain powers that do harm to the human body; and we shall not in every case accuse the soul of those who suffer, as though it were harmed by them. When the devil, having received authority to try Job through his body, struck him with an evil sore (Job 2:7), Job is not to be blamed for that; he contended and bravely endured the blow. Only, whenever we are tried by bodily pains, may it be said: “but do not [touch] his soul”, just as the Lord too, by rebuking, heals those who are sick.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 round 2: Pass B in the justification was a September summary ('infancy and forerunner'). The English is rewritten from the Greek: the Greek-order sentence 'May it not be, then, that in the…' is now plain English, and 'the whole wording', 'that could not withstand the power' and the closing gloss are restored.
After 'ἀλλὰ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ μὴ' the TEI has no verb; '[touch]' is supplied from Job 1:12 LXX (ἀλλ' αὐτοῦ μὴ ἅψῃ), which the edition's note cites.
'>᾿ ἀντὶ τοῦ >πέταξεν<' is read as '[ἐπετίμησεν] ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐπέταξεν': a lexical note that 'rebuked' stands for 'commanded'. The lemma word is supplied in brackets.
πράσει read φράσει (apparatus); 'καὶ καὶ' read once; 'τὸ τὸ διὰ' read 'τοῦ διὰ'.
